blocks.task_summary: (i) Estimate the probability that a randomly selected visitor will ride The Dragon, using the frequency table of 40 visitors. (ii) Estimate the expected number of times a visitor will ride The Dragon, using the same frequency table.
method_path: Sum non-zero frequencies or use complement to find number of riders: 1+16+13+2+3 = 34
Divide by total frequency to estimate P(rider) = 34/40
Set up expected value formula E(X) = sum of x*f_x/n using the frequency table

evidence.basis: summing frequencies of riders or finding complement (M1); probability = 34/40 (A1); attempt to find expected value (M1); (0*6 + 1*16 + 2*13 + 3*2 + 4*3)/40 = 60/40 = 1.5 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Given 1000 visitors and The Dragon carries a maximum of 10 people per run, estimate the minimum number of times The Dragon must run to satisfy demand, using the expected rides per visitor from part (a).
method_path: Multiply expected rides per visitor by number of visitors: 1.5 * 1000 = 1500 total expected rides
Divide total expected rides by ride capacity: 1500 / 10 = 150 runs

evidence.basis: evidence of their rides/visitor * 1000 or division by 10 (M1); 150 times (A1)
